items.title: Homebuilder Confidence Hits New 14-Year Low as High Mortgage Rates and Inflation Take a Toll
items.summary:
U.S. homebuilders are feeling increasingly pessimistic about the new-construction sector of the housing market amid mounting affordability concerns. 

Builder confidence in new single-family home sales fell three points month over month, bringing the National Association of Home Builders/Wells Fargo Housing Market Index (HMI) down to 25, a new 14-year low . Any reading below 50 reflects the industry's negative view of the market.

This is the lowest HMI reading since April 2012. For context, builder sentiment has now remained below 40 for 19 consecutive months.

NAHB Chairman Bill Owens attributes the sharp downturn to high mortgage rates, ongoing inflation pressure, elevated energy and material costs, rising labor shortages, and sidelined buyers.

"Builders are confronting multiple challenges in today’s economy," says Owens. "Stepped-up immigration enforcement is keeping legal workers off job sites, deepening labor shortages and driving up costs. Higher fuel prices are prompting subcontractors to raise their rates sharply, and with fewer buyers in the market, more builders are scaling back construction."

Last week, Freddie Mac reported that the average rate on 30-year fixed home loans decreased to 7.11%, tracking lower bond yields, yet the latest hotter-than-expected inflation print could make the relief short-lived.

NAHB chief economist Robert Dietz says that mortgage rates stuck above 7%, combined with weaker consumer confidence, and broader economic uncertainty are holding buyers back from the market, but that is just part of the problem. 

"The housing market faces…
items.t: Homebuilder Confidence Hits New 14-Year Low as High Mortgage Rates and Inflation Take a Toll

items.title: Home Depot Taps Longtime Exec for CEO as Company Faces ‘Frozen Housing Market’
items.summary:
Home Depot COO Richard McPhail was announced as the company's new CEO on Tuesday, ahead of the home improvement giant's third-quarter earnings call. McPhail will take over on Nov. 23.

McPhail is taking the reins from Ted Decker , who will stay on as chairman. Decker stepped into the role in 2022. 

McPhail has been with Home Depot since 2005 and previously served as executive vice president and chief financial officer.

Meanwhile, Ann-Marie Campbell was named president and chief operating officer. Campbell began her career with the retailer 41 years ago, as a sales associate and most recently served as an executive vice president in charge of U.S. stores as well as Home Depot Canada, Home Depot Mexico, and Pro sales and services.

On Tuesday, during its third-quarter earnings call , the company reported better than expected quarterly revenue of $43.4 billion, up 4.9% from a year ago.

In remarks during the call, McPhail said Home Depot is “continuing to gain market share in a pressured housing market."

During the company's second-quarter earnings call in August, McPhail spoke of the "consumer uncertainty" around the housing market.

"While consumer uncertainty and housing affordability continue to pressure demand for larger home improvement projects, we remain focused on what we can control, our strategy of driving our core and culture, delivering a frictionless, interconnected experience, and winning the pro," he said.

items.title: Builders Are Slashing Mortgage Rates To Win Buyers, but Hold Firm on Sticker Prices
items.summary:
Prices for new homes have been stagnant for years. That leaves room for potential homebuyers if they're on the hunt for good incentives.

The latest Realtor.com® quarterly construction insights report shows that prices on new homes are holding steady, but builders are having to get creative to attract buyers, relying on rate buydowns and other incentives as the 30-year fixed mortgage rate stays above 7% .

The median listing price for new builds hit $451,071 in the third quarter. It's been right around that number since late 2023. Builders are starting fewer homes in the inflation-plagued economy. 

Increased labor and material costs and decreased buyer demand led to the completion rate of new single-family homes falling 11.0% year over year in September.

Meanwhile, existing-home prices came in 1.5% below 2025 levels, landing at $402,883. New homes have to compete with existing homes for buyers, and the rise in existing-home sales shows that some cost-conscious buyers who might have built new are choosing existing, instead. Existing-home sales just hit a 16-year low .

"Builders were quicker to adjust to the realities of muted buyer demand in this high-rate environment, while existing-home sellers had pricing expectations based on the market from 2021 and 2022 that were slower to dissolve," Realtor.com senior economist Joel Berner writes in the report. "The overall price softness we’ve seen through 2026 is driven primarily by the existing-home segment."

That's led to more builders and sellers tempering their expectations. Resellers cut prices on 21.6% of homes this…
items.t: Builders Are Slashing Mortgage Rates To Win Buyers, but Hold Firm on Sticker Prices

items.title: Can America Build More Housing Without Gutting Historic Protections? Inside the Senate’s Permitting Battle
items.summary:
A sweeping permitting reform package moved closer to a final Senate vote Monday, when lawmakers voted 70–27 to limit debate on legislation that could weaken a federal safeguard for historic places.

At issue is Section 106 of the National Historic Preservation Act , which requires federal agencies to consider how projects they fund, approve, or permit might affect historic properties—and consult with those affected before proceeding.

The proposed changes would exempt most projects whose only federal connection is financial assistance, while imposing tighter deadlines and restricting legal challenges.

As the nation confronts a shortage of 4.03 million homes and an aging energy grid, supporters argue that reducing regulatory hurdles will accelerate infrastructure development. But preservation advocates warn the changes could leave communities with less influence over what gets built—and what gets lost.

"Preservation is not a hindrance to progress," Heather Veneziano , director of Tulane University's Historic Preservation Program , told Realtor.com® during a recent walking interview through Bayou St. John , one of New Orleans' oldest neighborhoods .

Rather than keeping neighborhoods frozen in time, she argued, preservation can help communities determine how they evolve.

"Keeping things static is impossible," Veneziano said.

Preserving the past without preventing the future 

New Orleans provides a particularly salient standpoint from which to understand Veneziano’s perspective.

The city is home to 26 nationally recognized historic districts encompassing more than…
items.t: Can America Build More Housing Without Gutting Historic Protections? Inside the Senate’s Permitting Battle

items.title: The Homeownership Gap Between Young and Old Americans Has Doubled—These Cities Reveal Why
items.summary:
The homeownership gap between younger and older Americans has more than doubled over the past four decades, with some of the nation's most expensive cities seeing the sharpest increases , according to a new report.

The analysis, from the Urban Institute , finds that nationally just 43% of households headed by adults aged 25 to 35 owned their homes in 2024, compared with 79% of those headed by adults 65 and older. The 35.8-percentage-point difference is more than twice the 17.5-point gap recorded in 1980.

But that divide pales in comparison to the gaping chasm in some of America's most expensive metropolitan areas. Between 1980 and 2024, the homeownership gap grew by 29 percentage points in Denver , 23 points in New York City , and 22 points in San Francisco , compared with 18.3 points nationally.

But those widening gaps also expose a deeper economic trade-off: The cities offering young Americans the greatest opportunities to earn more may be the very places preventing them from building wealth through homeownership

"The cities with the strongest labor markets tend to be the least affordable, so some will take the better job and rent indefinitely, giving up equity accumulation," explains Hannah Jones , senior economist at Realtor.com® . "Others will pass up higher-paying roles or move to cheaper, lower-opportunity markets in order to buy."

How Denver and New York arrived at the same divide 

In 1980, younger households in Denver were nearly as likely as their older counterparts to own a home.

At the time, 55% of households headed by adults aged 25 to 35 owned their…
items.t: The Homeownership Gap Between Young and Old Americans Has Doubled—These Cities Reveal Why

items.title: Aging Parents and Empty Nests Force Homeowners To Rethink Layouts Years Before the Move
items.summary:
Most homeowners know their homes may need updates to accommodate their changing needs as they age.

Some, however, are thinking even further ahead.

Instead of waiting until those changes are necessary, they’re investing in renovations years in advance to prepare for aging parents who might eventually move in after their children leave the nest.

Angi’s 2026 State of Home Spending Pulse study found that 66% of homeowners plan to make a major home investment within the next five years. And the 2027 Home Trends To Watch report predicts that 2027 will be the year they take a proactive approach and focus on creating a home that grows with them.

If you own your home, experts agree that you should anticipate how your needs could change in the next five to 10 years and use that information to guide your long-term home improvement goals today.

By doing so, you can make the most out of your renovation budget, avoid costly last-minute adjustments, and ensure your home comfortably adapts to the different stages of life.

What's driving this trend? 

Matt Plaskoff, CEO and founder of One Week Bath in Los Angeles , is seeing this proactive, multigenerational "future-proofing” trend among his clients. 

“It comes down to people having heard stories of it going the other way. Mom falls or receives a diagnosis, and suddenly the family is trying to put in a walk-in shower and grab bars on short notice while suddenly incurring more costs with doctors and insurance,” says Plaskoff.

Multigenerational living is also at an all-time high, and the recent National Association of Realtors®…
items.t: Aging Parents and Empty Nests Force Homeowners To Rethink Layouts Years Before the Move

items.title: Nantucket Brokerage Must Pay $1.3 Million to Buyers Who Couldn’t Expand Their Home as Desired
items.summary:
A Massachusetts judge and jury have ordered a Nantucket real estate firm to pay nearly $1.3 million to a couple after finding that one of its agents misrepresented whether a home could be expanded to fit their family of eight.

The yearslong legal battle centered on a twp-bedroom, 1,200 square-foot property purchased by Dr. Mary Murray and Jeff Ment. Murray, an obstetrician, and Ment, a lawyer, live in Westport, CT , but spend summers with their six children in Nantucket, MA.

Their kids “all love to be there. Every single one of them loves to be on the island, and we love to be with them,” Murray tells Realtor.com® . 

Their real estate agent, Melanie Gowen , helped them find rentals in previous years, and in 2020, she represented them in their purchase of 151 P olpis Road for $1.41 million. 

Murray says the home wasn’t ideal, but in the ultracompetitive Nantucket market, where the median listing price is $5,995,000, they felt lucky to buy anything at all. 

And Murray says the family was reassured after Gowen, an agent with William Raveis Nantucket, told the couple they’d have no problem building an addition to accommodate their six children. 

“She said, ‘Listen, I know it’s the smallest house, but it’s a great buy. The best part about this is it’s an undersized house on an oversized piece of property that you can double,’” Murray says. 

According to the couple, Gowen said she went to the island’s building department and confirmed expansion was possible. She’d even sketched out the addition and sent a video of the planned build, Murray says. 

In Nantucket, rules…
items.t: Nantucket Brokerage Must Pay $1.3M to Buyers Who Couldn’t Expand Their Home as Desired

items.title: Landlord With Dark Past Is Charged With the Murder of Disabled Tenant Who Was ‘Late on Rent’
items.summary:
A New Mexico landlord accused of murdering his disabled tenant and burying the body beneath the porch of the victim’s home gave conflicting accounts about whether he had evicted the man over purported unpaid rent, according to court documents.

Jonah Jeter , 33, was charged last week in Albuquerque with murder, aggravated burglary, and three counts of tampering with evidence in the death of Robert Debeary , 51, whose remains were discovered in October, more than two months after his family reported him missing.

For nearly five years, Debeary, a four-time stroke survivor, lived in an apartment at 233 Alcazar St. NE, where he received housing assistance through the federal Section 8 program, according to the criminal complaint filed in Bernalillo County Metropolitan Court.

Debeary, who walked with a cane after becoming paralyzed on one side of his body, regularly kept in touch with his loved ones, so when a week passed without hearing from him, his family grew concerned, according to his future daughter-in-law, Latajanae Evangelista , who spoke with Realtor.com® . 

In mid-August, Debeary’s brother contacted Albuquerque Community Safety to request a welfare check, but was told that he had been evicted from the apartment the previous week. His family questioned that account, saying he had never mentioned facing eviction despite complaining of “ongoing issues” with Jeter.

“He was just a man, a disabled man living in his home, and he would never just go missing. He would never leave his family,” Evangelista tells Realtor.com in a phone interview, her voice breaking as she…
items.t: Landlord With Dark Past Is Charged With the Murder of Disabled Tenant Who Was ‘Late on Rent’

New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye could miss the rest of the 2026 season after injuring his ankle against the Detroit Lions in Munich. (Matthew J. Lee/The Boston Globe via Getty Images) 

“The update that I have is just out of caution, Drake stayed back,” Vrabel said, as quoted by the Boston Herald’s Doug Kyed . “He’ll be traveling back here shortly. But just wanted to make sure that everything was good for him to travel back and safely. If Maye does end the season here, he will recover at his sprawling property, which his wife, Ann Michael , previously revealed a candid glimpse of.

items.title: Manhattan’s Top 2 Sales This Week Go Under Contract After Price Hikes
items.summary:
The top-two sales in Manhattan last week were in signature luxury buildings that have seen very strong sales and were able to raise their prices from initial launch.

The No. 1 contract, a 17th floor unit at 1122 Madison Ave. , is pending with an ask of $38.75 million, a bit over its original ask of $38 million in January. 

The next highest contact, Penthouse B at The Henry on 211 W. 84th St., went under contract with an ask of $28.75 million, a hefty bump over its August 2024 price tag of $24.95 million. 

Both units were sponsor sales in new construction, and are full-service luxury buildings with renowned architects and designers. The buildings essentially look at each other from across Central Park, one on the upper east side, one on the upper west.

"This is a sponsor strategy," says luxury broker Michael Reisor , of the Compass-affiliated Reisor.Team in Manhattan, who is familiar with both locations. "It's escalating pricing based on absorption."

Manhattan's No. 2 sale this week, Penthouse B at The Henry on 211 W. 84th St., went under contract with an ask of $28.75 million, a hefty bump over its August 2024 price tag of $24.95 million (Realtor.com)

items.title: Inside Harry Styles’ Multimillion-Dollar Property Portfolio as He’s Snubbed in the 2027 Grammy Nominations
items.summary:
Harry Styles was 18 when he reportedly bought his first house in North London. More than a decade later, the One Direction alum ’s real estate deals have taken him from a gated midcentury retreat in Los Angeles to one of Tribeca’s most star-studded condo buildings.

But some of his biggest purchases have brought him back to the same London neighborhood where he started. 

The singer was shut out of the 2027 Grammy nominations on Nov. 16, despite a year in which his fourth studio album—"Kiss All the Time. Disco, Occasionally.— reached No. 1 on the Billboard 200 and its lead single, “Aperture,” topped the Hot 100.

His previous album, "Harry’s House," won album of the year and best pop vocal album in 2023. 

Harry Styles was 18 when he reportedly bought his first house in North London. More than a decade later, the One Direction alum’s real estate deals have taken him from a gated midcentury retreat in Los Angeles to one of Tribeca’s most star-studded condo buildings. (Gareth Cattermole/Getty Images) 

The London neighborhood he kept buying in 

Styles’ first reported purchase was a white-stucco house near Hampstead Heath in 2012, when he was still in One Direction.

The house also has a home gym and a landscaped back garden. 

Several years later, Styles reportedly paid $11.6 million for another house in the area and $5.5 million for the adjoining…
items.t: Inside Harry Styles’ Multimillion-Dollar Property Portfolio as He’s Snubbed in the 2027 Grammy Nominations

items.title: Unlicensed Plumber Accused of Squatting and Subleasing Rooms in Senior Woman’s Home
items.summary:
A California woman who hired a plumber to make repairs to her home while she was living elsewhere says he took over the property, moved strangers into the house, and locked her out—sparking a two-year nightmare that left her fighting to reclaim her own home .

Jordy Smith , 76, said the man working on the plumbing at her home in San Diego's City Heights neighborhood allegedly transferred the utilities into his own name and began renting out rooms to strangers, pocketing the payments.

Smith and her partner, who owned the home, later discovered the man was not a licensed plumber; but by then, the situation had spiraled out of control. When the couple returned home, they were locked out of their own house and couldn’t get the new occupants to leave, she claimed. 

"He just took over and, like, before we knew it, there was like 15 people," Smith told ABC 10News . "Once that happened, it really made it look like to the homeless people that were coming in, that made it look like it was his house.”

The couple tried to confront the people living in the home but Smith said they had locked the door and wouldn’t talk. 

"I couldn't sleep at night," Smith said. "I mean, it just seemed like we'd never get back home."

Meanwhile, the property had attracted multiple visits by the police. San Diego police were called to the home more than 30 times between Jan. 1, 2024, and Aug. 17, 2026, for reports of suspected drug activity, trespassing, and smoke coming from the property, according to dispatch records. 

In an attempt to get the squatters removed from the property, Smith turned to…
items.t: Unlicensed Plumber Accused of Squatting and Subleasing Rooms in Senior Woman’s Home

items.summary:
Jenny McCarthy and Donnie Wahlberg have sold their Illinois residence for $2.6 million—two months after listing the sprawling St. Charles property for $2.8 million.

The singer , 57, and the actress, 53, owned the residence for more than a decade , having purchased it for $1.1 million in 2015.

Built in 1996, the four-bedroom, 5.5-bathroom home spans 7,236 square feet and sits on 1.26 acres.

Described as "an extraordinary St. Charles estate," the property underwent extensive renovations during Wahlberg and McCarthy's time there, with the couple transforming it into a personalized retreat designed for both entertaining and relaxing.

Inside, the home boasts an expansive living room and family room, a formal dining room, den, game room, recreation space, exercise room, and finished lower level.

The kitchen comes with an island, breakfast bar, walk-in pantry, and butler's pantry, while hardwood and stone flooring can be found throughout much of the main level.

items.title: Inside Dolly Parton’s Eclectic Property Portfolio and Legacy as the Music Legend Receives Posthumous Grammy Nods
items.summary:
Dolly Parton has left behind a legacy that will continue to grow for years to come. 

The music legend —who passed away following a brief battle with cancer at the age of 80 on Aug. 25—was recently honored by the Recording Academy, receiving three posthumous nominations ahead of the 69th Annual Grammy Awards. 

The "9 to 5" hitmaker has received two nominations in the Best Country/Duo Group Performance category for "Light of a Clear Blue Morning" with Lainey Wilson , Reba McEntire , Miley Cyrus , and Queen Latifah , and her "Butterfly" collaboration with the Zac Brown Band . 

Parton's memoir, "Star of the Show: My Life on Stage," has also received a nod in the Best Audio Book, Narration, and Storytelling Recording category. 

As Parton's contributions to the entertainment industry continue to receive their deserved recognition, it's worth noting another talent the country icon showcased throughout her lifetime: property investment.

Dolly Parton may have been known for her larger-than-life style and legendary music career, but the country music icon also quietly built up an impressive property portfolio over the decades. (Jeffrey Vest/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) 

To honor the country icon, Sept. 25 was hailed as "Dolly Parton day," and is set to be celebrated all across the country with parades, library fairs, community singing, and more.

items.title: Inside Warren Buffett’s Surprisingly Modest Property Portfolio as He Steps Down as Berkshire Hathaway Chairman
items.summary:
Billionaire investor Warren Buffett has officially stepped down as chairman of Berkshire Hathaway—marking the end of an extraordinary era for the 96-year-old businessman, whose approach to real estate has long been almost as unconventional as his investing career.

Berkshire Hathaway announced on Sept. 18 that Buffett has been named chairman emeritus, effective immediately, while his son, Howard G. Buffett , has been elected chairman of the board. Buffett will remain a director and continue to offer his insight to the company. 

“As Chairman Emeritus, Mr. Buffett will remain a member of the Board of Directors and will continue to offer his valued judgment and perspective,” Berkshire said.

The transition comes months after Buffett relinquished his CEO duties to longtime Berkshire executive Greg Abel , completing a carefully planned changing of the guard at the company Buffett has been associated with since 1965. Berkshire Hathaway sold $426 million more in stocks than it bought in the third quarter of 2026 under Abel. It was the 15th quarter out of the past 16 in which the company’s stock sales exceeded its purchases.

"I have served Berkshire since 1965," Buffett said in a letter to shareholders, released alongside the announcement. "Sixty-plus years in, I still have the best job in the world."

items.title: HOA Trade Group Presses for More Protections After DC Shooter Targeted Building Manager
items.summary:
The trade group representing homeowners associations is calling for stronger protections after a shooting in Washington, DC , left a community manager dead.

The Community Association Institute said that it would renew efforts support laws that address harassment, threats, and intimidation against community managers before they escalate into violence. 

The group had pressed for such legislation in Nevada in 2025 and plans to do so at the federal level in 2027. New Jersey and Minnesota are also reportedly considering some legislation to address harassment.

Thursday's shooting in DC's Logan Circle neighborhood claimed the life of James “Jimmy” Stuart , manager of the Metropole and injured five others. The suspected shooter, Dr. Matt Wade Lambert , a resident of the complex, reportedly was in a dispute with the community over renovations he said damaged his penthouse unit.

“We mourn Jimmy's loss and extend our deepest condolences to his family, friends, colleagues, and the entire Metropole community,” the CAI statement reads. “Our thoughts are also with the other victims, residents, and building staff whose lives have been forever changed by this tragedy.”

Lambert was in the middle of a protracted legal dispute with his building's HOA at the time that the shooting happened. 

Social median posts reputedly made by him criticized the community for months after he alleged repairs caused water damage and mold. Police say that, after Lambert killed Stuart and injured four others, he subsequently took his own life during a police standoff.

items.title: What Happened to Lindsay Clancy’s Home? How Duxbury House Was Quietly Sold to Former DA in Off-Market Deal Just a Year After Kids’ Deaths
items.summary:
Lindsay Clancy is set to face a second murder trial in March 2027—months after the jurors serving in the highly-publicized trial revealed they were deadlocked, forcing the judge to declare a mistrial, after an intense five-week courtroom showdown, during which they heard testimony from dozens of witnesses—and even visited the Massachusetts house where the former nurse is accused of murdering her children.

Clancy, 36, who did not testify in the case but was present in the Plymouth, MA , courtroom for the entirety of the trial, has admitted to taking the lives of daughter Cora , 5, and sons Dawson , 3, and 8-month-old Callan .

However, she pled not guilty to the three first-degree murder charges she is facing, alleging that she was suffering from severe postpartum psychosis at the time of their deaths. On Sept. 4, the judge declared a mistrial.

Now, it has been revealed that she will be back in court in March 2027 to face a retrial on the same charges. 

The trial began on July 31, when the jurors traveled to Clancy's former home in Duxbury, MA , where her three children were found in the basement by their father, Patrick Clancy , on Jan. 24, 2023, having been strangled with exercise bands. 

According to the Associated Press , the jury was escorted into the home in groups of six and spent a total of 40 minutes at the property, walking through the entire abode, as well as the yard where Clancy was found after throwing herself out of her bedroom window in an apparent suicide attempt. 

Lindsay Clancy is set to face a second murder trial in March 2027. (David L. Ryan/The…

‘We have further to go,’ says Huw Pill after increase to 4% this month as Bank seeks to tackle rising inflation

The Bank of England will probably need to raise interest rates next month and again in early 2027 to combat rising inflation, its chief economist has said.

Signalling a sharp rise in mortgage payments for an estimated 2.3 million homeowners who will have to refinance their loans next year, Huw Pill said that while the decision to nudge interest rates from 3.75% to 4% earlier this month was a “significant step” towards getting monetary policy into a better place, “we ⁠have further to go”.
